title: Firmus Saturninus, Proculus et Bonosus
author: Scriptores Historiae Augustae
source: Translated by Claude from phi2331.phi029.perseus-lat2, as held by the Perseus Digital Library.

passages.original: Fuit tamen Firmus statura ingenti, oculis foris eminentibus, capillo crispo, fronte vulnerata, vultu nigri ore, reliqua parte corporis candidus sed pilosus atque hispidus, ita ut eum plerique Cyclopem vocarent, carne multa vescebatur, struthionem ad diem comedisse fertur. vini non multum bibit, aquae plurimum, mente firmissimus, nervis robustissimus, ita ut Tritannum vinceret, cuius Varro meminit. nam et incudem superpositam pectori constanter aliis tundentibus pertulit, cum ipse reclinis ac resupinus et curvatus in manus penderet potius quam iaceret, fuit tamen ei contentio cum Aureliani ducibus ad bibendum, si quando eum temptare voluissent, nam quidam Burburus nomine de numero vexillariorum, notissimus potator, cum ad bibendum eundem provocasset, situlas duas plenas mero duxit et toto postea convivio sobrius fuit;
passages.english: Firmus, however, was of huge stature, with eyes bulging outward, curly hair, a scarred forehead, a face dark in complexion, and in the rest of his body white but hairy and shaggy, so that most people called him Cyclops. He ate a great deal of meat, and is said to have eaten an ostrich in a day. He drank not much wine but a great deal of water; he was very firm of mind and very strong of sinew, so that he outdid Tritannus, whom Varro mentions. For he also endured, steadily, an anvil placed on his chest while others hammered on it, when he himself, leaning back, face upward and arched, was hanging on his hands rather than lying down. He had, moreover, a contest in drinking with Aurelian's generals, whenever they wished to test him; for when a certain man named Burburus, from the ranks of the standard-bearers, a very well-known drinker, had challenged him to drink, he drained two buckets full of neat wine and was sober for the whole banquet afterwards;
passages.notes: "vultu nigri ore" is awkward and probably corrupt (perhaps for "vultu nigrior" or "vultu niger"); translated as "a face dark in complexion". "vexillarii" are soldiers serving under a vexillum (detachment standard), here rendered "standard-bearers".
